author: tp2836
body:
# Fix: Resolve BDD Test Failures with Undefined Steps and UI Filtering Issues

## Problem Statement

The BDD tests were failing with all scenarios marked as "error" or "undefined". Team members reported that `behave` tests were not passing, preventing proper validation of the UI functionality as required by Homework Requirement 4.

## Root Cause Analysis

After thorough investigation, identified multiple issues:

### 1. Missing Step Definitions
The feature file used step definitions that were completely undefined in the step files:
- `When I visit the "Home Page"`
- `When I press the "Search" button`
- `Given the following recommendations`
- `Then I should see "..." in the title`
- `Then I should see "..." in the results`
- `Then I should not see "..."`

### 2.UI Default Values Causing Unintended Filtering
The HTML form had default selections for dropdowns:
- `recommendation_type` defaulted to "accessory"
- `status` defaulted to "draft"

### 3. Brittle Test Assertions
Tests expected specific database IDs, but PostgreSQL uses auto-increment IDs that vary based on test execution order and database state.

### 4. Minor Text Mismatch
Expected page title: "Recommendations Demo RESTful Service"  
Actual page title: "Recommendations Demo REST API Service"

## Changes Made

### 1. `features/steps/web_steps.py`
- Added missing step definitions
- Modified `step_fill_field()` to handle both `<input>` and `<select>` elements
- Improved `step_verify_message()` with proper AJAX wait logic to ensure flash messages are loaded before verification

### 2. `features/steps/recommendations_steps.py`
- Implemented `@given('the following recommendations')` step definition
- Added logic to clear existing recommendations before each scenario
- Ensures test isolation by creating a clean database state
- Uses table data from feature file to populate test recommendations

### 3. `service/static/index.html`
- Fixed UI default filtering behavior

### 4. `features/recommendations.feature`
- Changed from ID-based assertion to name-based assertions (`"Phone X -> Case Y"`, `"Clothes X -> Clothes Y"`, etc.)
- Fixed page title expectation to match actual HTML
- Makes tests more resilient and business-focused

### Test Results
```
1 feature passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped
4 scenarios passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped
26 steps passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped
Took 1min 18.736s
```

author: copilot
body:
Built a React Native app for managing houseplants with watering schedule tracking and push notifications.

## Implementation

**UI & Styling**
- NativeWind (Tailwind CSS for React Native) configured with custom preset and metro bundler integration
- Reusable component library: Button (with variants), Card, PlantCard with status indicators
- React Navigation stack for PlantList ↔ AddPlant screens
- Status color coding: green (>2 days), orange (≤2 days), red (overdue)

**Plant Management**
- CRUD operations with AsyncStorage persistence
- Plant model: name, species, watering frequency, last/next watering dates, notes
- ID generation: `${Date.now()}-${Math.random().toString(36).substring(2, 11)}` to prevent collisions
- Automatic next-watering calculation on water action

**Notifications**
- Expo Notifications scheduled at 9 AM on watering day
- Skips scheduling for past dates to avoid invalid triggers
- Platform-specific permissions handling

## Key Files

```typescript
// src/types/plant.ts
interface Plant {
  id: string;
  name: string;
  wateringFrequency: number; // days
  lastWatered: string;
  nextWatering: string; // ISO date
}

// src/utils/plantUtils.ts
export const waterPlant = async (id: string) => {
  plant.lastWatered = now.toISOString();
  plant.nextWatering = calculateNextWatering(now, plant.wateringFrequency);
  await scheduleWaterReminder(plant);
}
```

## Screenshots

**Empty State**
![Empty State](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/66fb75d9-8651-4618-8df3-1f9dba99b0fb)

**Add Plant Form**
![Add Plant Form](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7cb8b891-1491-4005-8334-5b9abf4acf37)

**Plant List**
![Plant List](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/802bcab2-bf99-4ab0-90ae-f0d06b874892)

## Dependencies

```json
{
  "nativewind": "^4.x",
  "react-navigation": "^6.x",
  "@react-native-async-storage/async-storage": "^1.x",
  "expo-notifications": "~0.x",
  "lucide-react-native": "^0.x"
}
```

Cross-platform ready for iOS, Android, and Web.

author: copilot
body:
## Fix Forge Logic Bug - Prevent Multiple Repairs from Rapid Clicking ### Issue Fixed a bug where clicking the forge multiple times rapidly during the repair animation causes multiple swords to be created from a single broken weapon. ### Solution Implemented - [x] Explore repository structure and understand the codebase - [x] Test the game to reproduce and confirm the bug - [x] Add a repair state tracking system to prevent multiple simultaneous repairs - [x] Add a loading/progress bar during the forging process so players can see progress - [x] Implement clicker game mechanic - allow multiple clicks to speed up the repair progress - [x] Create an agent.md file with refactoring guidelines - [x] Test the fixes thoroughly - [x] Run code review and address feedback - [x] Run security scan - No vulnerabilities found - [x] Update agent.md based on review feedback - [x] Merge changes from main branch - [x] Implement accessibility and code quality improvements - [x] Refactor repair progress to be part of weapon state - [x] Add guidance on minimizing state management ### Changes Made #### 1. Fixed the Bug Added repair state tracking to prevent multiple simultaneous repairs. When a repair is in progress, additional clicks speed up the process instead of starting a new repair. #### 2. Added Progress Bar with Accessibility - Added HTML elements for a forge progress bar with ARIA attributes for screen reader support - Added CSS styling for the progress bar with smooth animations - Progress bar shows during the forging process with "Click to speed up!" message - Progress bar includes `role="progressbar"` and dynamic `aria-valuenow` updates for accessibility #### 3. Implemented Clicker Mechanic with Safeguards - Base repair time is 3 seconds - Each click during repair adds 100ms worth of progress (capped at 100% to prevent exceeding base time) - Visual feedback with hammer pulse animation on each helpful click (improved to prevent animation conflicts) - Progress updates smoothly at 50ms intervals - Animation state is checked via DOM classes rather than maintaining separate boolean flags #### 4. Refactored Architecture for Better Design **Major architectural improvement based on code review feedback:** - **Repair progress now belongs to the weapon itself** (stored in `GameState` as `weapon.repairProgress`) - **Forge only tracks which weapon it's currently working on** (via `forgeState.currentWeaponId`) - This design follows single responsibility principle - weapons own their repair state, the forge is just a tool that modifies it - Added `getWeaponById()`, `updateWeaponProgress()`, and `getWeaponProgress()` methods to `GameState` - Renamed `repairState` to `forgeState` in UI module to clarify its purpose - Improved code maintainability and scalability for future features **Architecture Diagram:** Before (UI owned repair state): ``` UI Module ├── repairState { progress, weaponId, ... } └── GameState.getSelectedWeapon() ``` After (Weapon owns repair state): ``` GameState ├── weapons[].repairProgress ✓ (progress lives in weapon) └── UI Module └── forgeState { currentWeaponId } (forge tracks what it's working on) ``` #### 5. Created and Refined agent.md Comprehensive refactoring guidelines updated based on feedback: - Allow removing/replacing code when it's better or no longer necessary - Clarified file size thresholds: plan new modules at 200+ lines, split files at 300+ lines - Added guidance to review structure when adding new modules/files - Emphasized PURE functions and clean state management - Converted negative anti-patterns to positive prompting - Ensured README verification is included - Removed "bad approach" sections for clearer guidance - **Added guidance on minimizing unnecessary state management** (Latest Update): - Prefer calculated values over flags - Emphasize single source of truth - Avoid state that needs to be kept in sync - Use DOM state where appropriate instead of duplicating in JS - Added practical example scenario showing how to check animation state via DOM classes instead of boolean flags #### 6. Code Quality Improvements - Extracted magic numbers to named constants - Added CSS custom property for progress transition duration - Improved code readability and maintainability - Capped progress value to prevent exceeding 100% with rapid clicks - Added ARIA attributes to progress bar for screen reader accessibility - Improved animation handling to prevent conflicts with rapid clicks (checks DOM classes instead of maintaining separate flags) - Increased completion message delay from 1s to 1.5s for better visibility #### 7. Merged Changes from Main - Integrated GitHub Pages link added to README - Ensured all main branch changes are included ### Screenshots **Refactored architecture working correctly:** **Progress bar with accessibility support:** **Completed repair (only 1 sword created from rapid clicks):** ### Testing Results ✅ Bug fixed: Rapid clicking no longer creates multiple items ✅ Progress bar displays correctly with accessibility support ✅ Clicker mechanic works: Multiple clicks speed up repair (capped at 100%) ✅ Only one item is added to inventory per weapon repaired ✅ Animation improvements prevent conflicts with rapid clicks ✅ **Repair progress now properly belongs to weapons, not the forge** ✅ Forge correctly tracks which weapon it's working on ✅ Cleaner architecture with better separation of concerns ✅ Animation state managed via DOM classes (single source of truth) ✅ All existing functionality preserved ✅ Code review feedback addressed ✅ Security scan passed - No vulnerabilities found ✅ Agent.md updated per review feedback including state management guidance ✅ Main branch changes merged successfully ### Technical Details **GameState Changes:** - Added `repairProgress` property to weapon objects - Added `getWeaponById()` to retrieve weapons by ID - Added `updateWeaponProgress()` to update weapon repair progress - Added `getWeaponProgress()` to retrieve weapon repair progress - Weapons now initialize with `repairProgress: 0` when created **UI Module Changes:** - Renamed `repairState` to `forgeState` for clarity - Simplified forge state to only track `currentWeaponId` and `progressInterval` - Removed local progress tracking - now delegates to GameState - Updated all repair logic to read/write weapon progress via GameState methods - Forge ignores clicks on different weapons while repairing one - Animation state checked via `classList.contains()` instead of maintaining separate boolean - follows principle of calculated values over flags **Agent.md Updates:** - Added State Management principles emphasizing: - Minimize unnecessary state management - Prefer calculated values over flags - Single source of truth for each piece of data - Solutions should be easy to keep in sync - Added Scenario 4 demonstrating how to check animation state via DOM classes instead of using boolean flags - This guidance helps maintain cleaner, more maintainable code with fewer synchronization issues This refactoring follows the principles of **single responsibility**, **minimal state management**, and **single source of truth** - weapons own their repair state, the forge is just a tool that modifies it, and animation state is determined by checking the DOM rather than duplicating it in JavaScript. - Fixes UnbrokenTechnology/clicker-forge#4

author: bennybp
body:
A few times I've tried to do the generally-recognized standard

```
import basis_set_exchange as bse
bse.version()
```

However, that version function corresponds to the importlib version function, which requires the distribution name.

This fixes that so any of the following will work

```
import basis_set_exchange as bse
bse.version()
bse.get_version()
bse.api.version()
```

with the `bse.get_version` and `bse.api.version()` staying purely for backwards compatibility

author: maxencebernardhub
body:
## Summary

This PR introduces full support for the **CA ASPE** accounting standard in SMB FinSight and prepares the project for multi-standard usage alongside FR PCG.

## Changes

- Added CA ASPE income statement mapping:
  - `mapping/income_statement_ca_aspe.csv`
- Added CA ASPE-specific ratios rules:
  - `ratios/ratios_ca_aspe.toml`
- Added generic CA ASPE chart of accounts template:
  - `data/reference/ca_aspe.csv`
- Added CA ASPE sample accounting entries:
  - `data/input/accounting_entries_ca_aspe.csv`
- Added standard-specific configuration for CA ASPE:
  - `config/standard_ca_aspe.toml`
- Updated global configuration to support multiple standards (FR PCG + CA ASPE):
  - `smb_finsight_config.toml`
- Updated README:
  - Documented multi-standard support (FR PCG and CA ASPE)
  - Updated project structure, roadmap and version history
- Bumped version to **0.2.0**:
  - `pyproject.toml`
  - `smb_finsight/__init__.py`

## Technical details

- CA ASPE mapping covers all relevant P&L accounts (4xxx → 8xxx) with no overlaps.
- Ratios file (`ratios_ca_aspe.toml`) includes:
  - Derived measures (gross margin, EBITDA, ROE, ROA, ROCE, DSO/DPO/DIO, etc.)
  - Basic / advanced / full ratio levels, aligned with the FR PCG standard.
- New CA ASPE COA (`ca_aspe.csv`) is a generic template that remains compatible with the mapping patterns.
- Sample entries are provided for CA ASPE to generate a full income statement and ratios out of the box.

## Testing

- Ran CLI with CA ASPE standard:
  - `--scope statements` (simplified / regular / complete views)
  - `--scope ratios` (basic / full levels)
  - Mixed scopes (`--scope all`) with different periods:
    - FY / YTD / MTD / last-month
    - custom date ranges
- Verified:
  - No unmapped accounts for CA ASPE sample entries
  - No overlapping accounts in the mapping
  - All ratios compute successfully when required balance sheet measures are available

## Checklist

- [x] Code compiles and CLI runs with `CA_ASPE` standard
- [x] Mapping and ratios for CA ASPE are complete and consistent
- [x] README updated (features, standards, structure, roadmap)
- [x] Version bumped to **0.2.0**

author: azizmazrou
body:
This commit addresses the issue of hardcoded URLs in the OpenAPI schema by making all API endpoints fully configurable through environment variables.

## Problem Solved
Previously, the OpenAPI schema had hardcoded URLs:
- http://localhost:8000
- http://ews-mcp:8000

This was inflexible for:
- Production deployments behind reverse proxies
- Custom domains and different network configurations
- Cloud deployments (AWS, Azure, GCP)
- Multiple environments (dev, staging, production)

## Changes Made

### 1. Configuration (src/config.py)
- Added `API_BASE_URL` - External/public API URL
- Added `API_BASE_URL_INTERNAL` - Internal Docker network URL
- Added `API_TITLE`, `API_DESCRIPTION`, `API_VERSION` - Customizable metadata
- Added `get_api_base_urls()` method with smart defaults

### 2. OpenAPI Adapter (src/openapi_adapter.py)
- Updated constructor to accept optional settings parameter
- Modified `generate_openapi_schema()` to use dynamic URLs from settings
- Falls back to sensible defaults if not configured
- Uses configured port from MCP_PORT setting

### 3. Main Server (src/main.py)
- Pass settings to OpenAPIAdapter during initialization
- Updated log message to indicate dynamic configuration

### 4. Docker Compose (docker-compose.openwebui.yml)
- Added new environment variables section for API configuration
- Documented with inline comments and examples
- All variables optional with smart defaults

### 5. Documentation (OPENWEBUI_SETUP.md)
- Added comprehensive "Configurable API URLs" section
- Included use cases for different deployment scenarios
- Examples for Nginx reverse proxy, cloud deployment, multi-env
- Updated Open WebUI integration instructions

### 6. Example Config (.env.example)
- Added new API configuration variables (commented out)
- Clear examples for different use cases

## Environment Variables

**New variables (all optional):**
```env
API_BASE_URL=https://ews-api.company.com
API_BASE_URL_INTERNAL=http://ews-mcp:8000
API_TITLE=My Company Exchange API
API_DESCRIPTION=Custom API description
API_VERSION=1.0.0
```

**Defaults if not set:**
- URLs: http://localhost:{MCP_PORT}, http://ews-mcp:{MCP_PORT}
- Title: "Exchange Web Services (EWS) MCP API"
- Description: "REST API for Exchange operations via Model Context Protocol"
- Version: "3.0.0"

## Use Cases

1. **Behind Reverse Proxy:** API_BASE_URL=https://api.company.com/ews

2. **Cloud Deployment:** API_BASE_URL=https://ews-api.us-east-1.mycloud.com

3. **Custom Docker Network:** API_BASE_URL_INTERNAL=http://exchange-api:9000

4. **Multiple Environments:**
   - Dev: http://localhost:8000
   - Staging: https://ews-api-staging.company.com
   - Production: https://ews-api.company.com

## Benefits

✅ Flexible deployment configurations
✅ No hardcoded URLs
✅ Backward compatible (uses smart defaults)
✅ Supports multiple environments
✅ Works with any reverse proxy setup
✅ Cloud-ready architecture
✅ Comprehensive documentation

## Testing

Test the configuration:
```bash
# Set custom URL
export API_BASE_URL=https://my-api.com
# Start server
./start-openwebui.sh
# Check OpenAPI schema
curl http://localhost:8000/openapi.json | jq '.servers'
```

This makes the EWS MCP server truly production-ready with enterprise-grade flexibility!

author: shigeo-isshiki
body:
Updated the README to reflect changes in the project structure, added documentation for new utilities, and provided instructions for local development and CI troubleshooting.

## 概要

（変更内容を短くまとめてください — 例: 「`.gitattributes` を追加して EOL を LF に正規化」「Husky pre-commit の実行ビットを index に記録」「Puppeteer デバッグスクリプトを追加」）

## 変更の目的

- なぜこの変更が必要か（背景、問題点、改善点）を記載してください。

## 確認チェックリスト

- [ ] 変更は小さく、目的が明確である（大きい変更は分割を検討）
- [ ] 既存の機能に影響がない（互換性の破壊がある場合は明示）
- [ ] `.gitattributes` を追加/変更した場合は、renormalize を行いましたか？（例: `git add --renormalize .` の結果を確認）
- [ ] Husky のフック実行ビットを index に記録した場合はその理由を記載しましたか？（例: `.husky/pre-commit` が実行されることを確認済み）
- [ ] 依存関係をインストールして lint/staged が動くことを確認しましたか？（`npm ci` -> 変更をステージ -> `git commit` で確認）
- [ ] `npm run ci-check`（prepare:dist, window VM check, puppeteer-check）やプロジェクトの CI スクリプトが通ることを確認しましたか？
- [ ] 主要な静的チェック（`npm run lint` / `npm run lint:ci`）を通過しましたか？
- [ ] 変更による UI/機能の影響がある場合、再現手順とスクリーンショット/ログを添付しましたか？
- [ ] ドキュメント（README、CHANGELOG、PR 本文）を更新しましたか？
- [ ] Windows を使う開発者向けの注意点があれば記載しましたか？（例: `npm ci` を実行する、必要なら `git update-index --chmod=+x .husky/pre-commit`）

## テスト手順（レビュワー向け）

1. ブランチをチェックアウト:

   ```bash
   git fetch origin
   git checkout <このブランチ名>
   ```

2. 依存をインストール:

   ```bash
   npm ci
   ```

3. 自動チェックを実行（任意だが推奨）:

   ```bash
   npm run lint:ci
   npm run prepare:dist
   npm run ci-check
   ```

4. フック確認（Husky）:

   - 空コミットで pre-commit が起動することを確認する:

     ```bash
     git commit --allow-empty -m "test: husky"
     ```

   - または小さな変更をステージして通常コミットし、`lint-staged` による自動整形が行われることを確認してください。

## 影響範囲 / リスク

- `.gitattributes` による影響（行末の正規化で差分が出る場合があるため、レビュー時に差分を注意深く確認してください）。
- Husky の実行フラグはプラットフォーム依存の扱いがある（Windows では FS の実行権限概念が異なります）。

## 関連チケット / 参考

- 関連する issue や外部参照があればリンクを貼ってください。

---

（このテンプレートはチームのベストプラクティスに合わせて調整してください。必要なら英文版も用意します）
## 概要

この PR が何を変更するかを簡潔に記載してください（例: README 更新、バグ修正、機能追加など）。

## 変更内容
- 変更したファイルの一覧と短い説明を箇条書きで書いてください。

## 必須チェックリスト (作成者用)
下の項目を確認してから PR を作成してください。

- [ ] ローカルで `npm ci` を実行し、依存が最新であることを確認した
- [ ] `npm run lint` を実行してエラーがないことを確認した（必要なら `npm run lint:fix` を実行）
- [ ] `npm run format` を実行してコードを整形した（またはコミット前フックで自動整形されることを確認）
- [ ] (必要時) `npm run prepare:dist` と `npm run zip` を実行して `package.zip` を確認した
- [ ] レビュワーに @mention してレビューを依頼した


## 確認手順（レビュワー向け）
1. ローカルで依存をインストール: `npm ci`
2. コミット前フック（husky + lint-staged）が有効になっていることを確認します（通常は `npm ci` で自動設定されます）。
3. 必要に応じてローカルでフォーマットと lint を実行:
   - `npm run format`（任意）
   - `npm run lint`（エラーがないか確認）
4. (変更がビルド対象の場合) `npm run prepare:dist` → `npm run zip` を実行して `package.zip` を確認します。

## CI チェック
- 本リポジトリでは PR 作成時に以下が自動実行されます:
  - Prettier のフォーマットチェック
  - ESLint の実行
  - (定義があれば) `npm test`
  - `prepare:dist` とパッケージの作成

CI が失敗した場合は、Actions のログを確認し、README の「よくある CI 失敗例と対処法」を参照してください。

## レビュアーへの依頼
- レビューを依頼したい人を @mention してください（例: `@team`）。
- レビューで特に見てほしい点があれば記載してください。

## 備考
- この PR に関する補足情報（関連 Issue 番号、スクリーンショット、注意点など）があれば記載してください。

author: aaronsteers
body:
## What

Fixes the Kotlin Bulk CDK Documentation workflow failing on master branch with error:
```
fatal: not a git repository (or any of the parent directories): .git
##[error]The process '/usr/bin/git' failed with exit code 128
```

**Failed run:** https://github.com/airbytehq/airbyte/actions/runs/19578468640

**Requested by:** AJ Steers (@aaronsteers)  
**Devin session:** https://app.devin.ai/sessions/f46b19703bd848dbad2c58cb105d470a

## How

Added `actions/checkout@v4` step with `fetch-depth: 0` to the `detect-changes` job before running `dorny/paths-filter@v3.0.2`.

**Root cause:** The `dorny/paths-filter` action behaves differently on `pull_request` vs `push` events:
- On `pull_request` events: Uses GitHub API to detect changes (no local git repo needed)
- On `push` events: Runs git commands locally (requires a checked-out repository)

The workflow worked on PRs but failed on master because the `detect-changes` job had no checkout step.

## Review guide

1. **`.github/workflows/kotlin-bulk-cdk-dokka-publish.yml` lines 25-28**: Verify the checkout step is correctly placed before the paths-filter action
2. **`fetch-depth: 0`**: Confirm this is appropriate for paths-filter to detect changes (it needs git history)
3. **Potential issue**: Verify that the GitHub variable `VERCEL_KOTLIN_CDK_PROJECT_ID` is configured in the repository settings (line 86, 90). If not configured, the Vercel deployment will silently skip.

## User Impact

**Positive:**
- The Kotlin Bulk CDK documentation workflow will now run successfully on master branch pushes
- Documentation will be automatically deployed to production on master merges

**Negative:**
- None expected. The checkout step adds minimal overhead (~1-2 seconds)

## Can this PR be safely reverted and rolled back?

- [x] YES 💚

Reverting would return the workflow to its broken state on master, but would not affect any other functionality. The workflow would continue to work on PRs (using GitHub API) but fail on master pushes.

I suggest this change because the Bitnami Kafka image is now behind a paywall and no longer publicly available, which prevents CI/CD and local environments from functioning properly.

The Soldevelo Kafka image is a drop-in replacement that remains fully compatible with Bitnami's configuration and environment variables. It's actively maintained and provides the same functionality.

body:
### Goal
Implement comprehensive reverse proxy hardening by deploying OWASP Juice Shop behind Nginx with security headers, TLS encryption, and rate limiting - all without modifying application code.
### Changes
- **Infrastructure**: Deployed Docker Compose stack with Nginx reverse proxy and Juice Shop backend
- **Security Headers**: Added 8 security headers (X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options, HSTS, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, COOP, CORP, CSP-Report-Only)
- **TLS Encryption**: Configured TLS 1.2/1.3 with strong cipher suites and self-signed certificates
- **Rate Limiting**: Implemented request throttling (10r/m with burst=5) on login endpoints
- **Timeouts**: Set comprehensive timeout policies to mitigate DoS/slowloris attacks
### Testing
- **Protocol Verification**: Confirmed only TLS 1.2/1.3 enabled via testssl.sh scan
- **Header Validation**: Verified security headers present on HTTP/HTTPS responses
- **HSTS Enforcement**: Confirmed HSTS header appears only on HTTPS (not HTTP redirects)
- **Rate Limit Testing**: Successfully triggered 429 responses after exceeding threshold (6/12 requests blocked)
- **Vulnerability Scan**: Validated no known TLS vulnerabilities (Heartbleed, POODLE, BEAST, etc.)
### Artifacts & Screenshots
- **Security Scans**: `analysis/testssl.txt`
- **Header Verification**: `analysis/headers-http.txt`, `analysis/headers-https.txt`
- **Rate Limit Testing**: `analysis/rate-limit-test.txt`
- **Documentation**: Complete lab submission in `labs/submission11.md`

author: jmartin-tech
body:
Allow generators in each process to create `repeatable` pseudo random values. This allows users more repeatability when generators use random values for request parameters. PRNG access across various processes is not `synchronized` meaning this will not produce 100% predictable random values for all cases. The primary target is to isolate randomness during generation for an individual attempt when `parallel_attempts` is enabled.

Note if `parallel_requests` is used the instance PRNG object is not reinitialized for each request.

* seed instance PRNG during generations loop
* update all generator `random` access to used instance PRNG

## Verification

List the steps needed to make sure this thing works

- [ ] `garak -t nim -n <model_name>`
- [ ] **Verify** across multiple runs requests for each attempt provides consistent `seed` and `temperature` values for repeated generations of `attempt.prompt`. 
- [ ] Run the tests and ensure they pass `python -m pytest tests/`

author: copilot
body:
REST API validation rejected assistant messages with `null` content, causing `messages[N][content] does not match any of the expected formats` errors. OpenAI's API uses `null` content for assistant messages containing tool_calls without text.

## Changes

**REST API Schema** (`includes/rest/class-wp-mcp-ai-rest-chat-controller.php`)
- Added `array('type' => 'null')` to content field `oneOf` schema in both chat and transcript endpoints
- Allows assistant messages to have null content when tool_calls are present

**Test Coverage** (`tests/test-rest-validator.php`)
- Added validation tests for null content scenarios
- Covers both explicit `content: null` and omitted content field for assistant role

**Tool Visibility** (`assets/js/chat.js`)
- Changed `extractGenericToolResponse()` to return generic success message instead of null for tools without specific output
- Maintains agentic loop visual continuity; all tool executions now show user feedback

## Example

Frontend sends conversation with tool calls:
```javascript
{
  messages: [
    { role: "user", content: "Generate an image" },
    { role: "assistant", content: null, tool_calls: [{...}] },  // ← Previously rejected
    { role: "tool", tool_call_id: "call_123", content: "{...}" }
  ]
}
```

Schema now validates this message format correctly, matching OpenAI's specification.

> The advanced tests are breaking on this PR because they are broken on main right now. These advanced tests will be fixed when #683 is merged. Then we can merge main on this PR and check that nothing is additionally broken.

## Summary of changes and related issue
Refactor / modify `get_closest_gridcell` and `get_closest_gridcells` in `climakitae.util.utils`.

## Relevant motivation and context
Previous logic snapped the input lat/lon to the grid of the dataset, but neglected to validate the data at that point was valid. 

This update snaps to the grid, checks if the data at that gridcell is valid, if it is it returns that gridcell, if not it searches the surrounding 8 gridcells for valid data. If any of the surrounding cells have valid data, all valid cells data is averaged and returned as if it were the requested gridcell. If none of the surrounding cells are valid an empty cell is returned.

Make sure all the tests are running successfully. Then load the attached notebook into jupyterhub, check out this branch, and run. Please play around with it a bit and try to break it if you can. This function is everywhere and we don't have smoke tests for notebooks yet.

author: seijikohara
body:
## Summary

This PR enhances the TypeScript type system and ESLint configuration to improve code quality, type safety, and maintainability across the codebase. The changes align with Vue 3.5 Composition API best practices and modern TypeScript patterns.

## Changes

### Type System Improvements
- **Environment Variables**: Strengthen type definitions with literal union types for `VUE_APP_HISTORY_MODE` (`'hash' | 'history'`)
- **Vite Environment**: Add comprehensive type definitions for Vite's built-in environment variables (`MODE`, `DEV`, `PROD`, `SSR`)
- **Constant Types**: Add `readonly` modifiers and use `as const` for immutable data structures

### ESLint Configuration Enhancements
- **Vue 3 Priority A (Essential)**:
  - `vue/require-v-for-key`: Enforce key attribute on v-for directives
  - `vue/no-use-v-if-with-v-for`: Prevent v-if/v-for conflicts
  - `vue/require-prop-types`: Require explicit prop types
  
- **Vue 3 Priority B (Strongly Recommended)**:
  - Component naming conventions (PascalCase)
  - HTML self-closing tag rules
  - Attribute ordering and formatting
  - Template structure guidelines
  
- **Vue 3.5 Composition API**:
  - Enable props destructuring (`vue/no-setup-props-destructure: off`)
  - Configure macro ordering (`defineOptions`, `defineModel`, `defineProps`, etc.)
  - Enforce `vue/prefer-define-options` for component options
  - Set preferred block order (script/template first, style last)

### Code Quality Improvements
- **Props Handling**: Refactor from `withDefaults(defineProps())` to direct destructuring for better readability
- **Type Safety**: Leverage TypeScript's `satisfies` keyword for better type inference without widening
- **Router**: Simplify history creation with type-safe lookup pattern using `Record` and type guards
- **Code Cleanup**: Remove redundant JSDoc comments that duplicate self-evident code functionality
- **Array Bounds**: Add proper bounds checking in `formatBytes` to prevent array overflow
- **Ace Config**: Extract ace.config setup to separate module to prevent re-initialization

### Dependency Updates
- TypeScript ESLint: `8.46.4` → `8.47.0`
- Vite: `7.2.2` → `7.2.4`
- @vitejs/plugin-vue: `6.0.1` → `6.0.2`
- @tsconfig/node22: `22.0.4` → `22.0.5`
- sass: `1.94.0` → `1.94.2`
- marked: `17.0.0` → `17.0.1`
- json-tree-view-vue3: `1.0.2` → `1.1.2` (with CSS import path fix)

## Technical Details

### Type Safety Pattern Examples

**Before:**
```typescript
const props = withDefaults(defineProps<Props>(), {
  mode: 'json',
  theme: 'monokai'
})
```

**After:**
```typescript
const { mode = 'json', theme = 'monokai' } = defineProps<Props>()
```

**Type-Safe Router History:**
```typescript
const historyCreators = {
  hash: () => createWebHashHistory(),
  history: () => createWebHistory(import.meta.env.BASE_URL),
} as const satisfies Record<string, () => RouterHistory>
```

**Array Bounds Checking:**
```typescript
const i = Math.min(Math.floor(Math.log(bytes) / Math.log(BYTE_BASE)), BYTE_SIZES.length - 1)
```

**Ace Config Module Separation:**
```typescript
// src/config/ace.ts - runs once at module load
ace.config.setModuleUrl('ace/mode/json_worker', workerJsonUrl)
```

## Review Feedback Addressed

All Copilot review comments have been addressed:
1. ✅ **tsconfig.app.json**: Kept `baseUrl` removed (deprecated in TS 7.0, works with Bundler resolution)
2. ✅ **formatBytes**: Added array bounds checking with `Math.min()`
3. ✅ **CodeEditor**: Extracted ace.config to separate module
4. ✅ **Build Failure**: Updated json-tree-view-vue3 to 1.1.2 with correct CSS import path

## Testing

- [x] Type checking passes (`vue-tsc`)
- [x] ESLint passes without errors
- [x] Build completes successfully
- [x] Vercel deployment successful
- [x] All functionality tested

## Breaking Changes

None. All changes maintain backward compatibility.

## CI Status

- ✅ Type checking: Passed
- ✅ ESLint: Passed
- ✅ Build: Passed
- ✅ Vercel deployment: Success

author: kuderr
body:
## Summary

This PR adds comprehensive planning documentation for a new **Settings feature** that will provide Pydantic Settings-like functionality for application configuration management in Classno.

## Changes

- **Created** `docs/settings-feature.md` - 17KB detailed feature specification including:
  - Architecture overview with ConfigSource abstraction
  - Implementation roadmap (phased approach)
  - Detailed usage examples and API design
  - Integration strategy with existing features
  - Dependencies and compatibility considerations
  
- **Updated** `TODO.md` - Added Settings feature reference under "Medium Priority → Features & Functionality" with quick overview and link to detailed docs

## Feature Overview

The planned Settings feature will enable:

✅ **Environment variable loading** with prefix support (`__env_prefix__`)  
✅ **Multiple config file formats** - JSON, YAML, TOML, .env  
✅ **Pluggable ConfigSource abstraction** for custom sources (Redis, AWS SSM, etc.)  
✅ **Secret field handling** - sensitive data hidden in repr  
✅ **Nested configuration models** with automatic prefix propagation  
✅ **Seamless integration** with existing VALIDATION and LOSSY_AUTOCAST features  
✅ **Zero required dependencies** - stdlib only (optional: python-dotenv, PyYAML, tomli)  

## Example Usage (Planned)

```python
from classno import Classno, Features, field

class Settings(Classno):
    __features__ = Features.SETTINGS | Features.VALIDATION
    __env_prefix__ = "APP_"
    __config_file__ = "config.json"
    
    debug: bool = field(default=False)
    database_url: str = field(metadata={"env": "DATABASE_URL", "secret": True})

# Automatically loads from environment, config files, and defaults
settings = Settings()
```

## Why This Matters

This feature will make Classno a viable alternative to Pydantic Settings for configuration management while maintaining zero required dependencies and leveraging Classno's existing validation and type casting capabilities.

## Next Steps

This PR contains **planning documentation only** - no code changes. Implementation can be tracked against the detailed specification in `docs/settings-feature.md`.

## Test Plan

- [x] Documentation is clear and comprehensive
- [x] TODO.md properly references the new feature
- [x] No code changes - documentation only

body:
Implements serverless deployment for 10 Moral Compass Gradio applications using Google Cloud Run's "build once, deploy many" pattern. Single Docker image (~500MB) deployed to 10 services differentiated by `APP_NAME` environment variable.

## Implementation

**`launch_entrypoint.py`** - Entry point with lazy import routing
```python
app_name = os.environ.get("APP_NAME", "tutorial")
if app_name == "tutorial":
    from aimodelshare.moral_compass.apps.tutorial import create_tutorial_app as factory
elif app_name == "judge":
    from aimodelshare.moral_compass.apps.judge import create_judge_app as factory
# ... 8 more apps
demo = factory()
demo.launch(server_name="0.0.0.0", server_port=port, analytics_enabled=False)
```

**`Dockerfile`** - Python 3.9 slim base with optimized layering
- System deps: libgl1-mesa-glx, libglib2.0-0 for matplotlib/seaborn
- Requirements copied first for Docker cache efficiency
- Port 8080 exposure for Cloud Run compatibility

**`requirements-apps.txt`** - Dependency optimization
- Excludes: TensorFlow (~2GB), PyTorch (~1GB) 
- Includes: onnx/onnxruntime (~200MB) - required for model_building_game Competition feature
- Result: 83% size reduction vs full ML stack

**`.github/workflows/deploy_gradio_apps.yml`** - CI/CD automation
- Job 1: Build single image, push to Artifact Registry
- Job 2: Matrix deploy to 10 services in parallel
- Flags: `--concurrency=80 --session-affinity --min-instances=0 --max-instances=50`

**`tests/test_launch_entrypoint.py`** - Validation suite
- Factory function existence and callability
- Import routing for all 10 apps
- Dockerfile and requirements structure

## Architecture

- **Cold start**: <5s (vs 15-30s with TensorFlow/PyTorch)
- **Scaling**: 0-50 instances per service, 80 concurrent connections each
- **Session affinity**: Maintains Gradio state across multi-step interactions
- **Cost**: Pay-per-use, scales to zero

## Deployment

Requires GCP setup: Artifact Registry repository, service account with Cloud Run Admin + Artifact Registry Writer roles. GitHub secrets: `GCP_PROJECT_ID`, `GCP_SA_KEY`. See `CLOUD_RUN_DEPLOYMENT.md` for complete instructions.

Apps deployed: tutorial, judge, ai-consequences, what-is-ai, model-building-game, ethical-revelation, moral-compass-challenge, bias-detective, fairness-fixer, justice-equity-upgrade.

Please follow these instructions to create PR to move each of our gradio apps to google cloud run:

This document outlines the strategy for migrating the "Moral Compass" Gradio applications from ephemeral notebook environments to a robust, serverless **Google Cloud Run** architecture.

### **Goal 1: Massive Scalability (1,000+ Concurrent Students)**
* **Problem:** Colab/Notebooks cannot handle simultaneous traffic from a large class.
* **Solution:** Cloud Run automatically scales the number of server instances up and down based on traffic.
* **Optimization:** By configuring **Session Affinity**, we ensure that a student's interaction (e.g., clicking "Next" in a multi-step app) stays connected to the same server, preventing state loss.

### **Goal 2: High Performance & Fast "Cold Starts"**
* **Problem:** Standard ML Docker images are massive (3GB+) due to TensorFlow and PyTorch, leading to slow startup times (15-30s) when a new server spins up.
* **Solution:** We implement a **"Lite" dependency strategy**. Since the "Moral Compass" apps are educational UIs (logic/text/charts) and do not perform heavy training, we explicitly **exclude** `tensorflow`, `torch`, and `onnx`.
* **Result:** Container size drops to ~300MB, allowing apps to boot in **<3 seconds**.

### **Goal 3: Cost Efficiency**
* **Architecture:** We use a **"Build Once, Deploy Many"** pattern.
    * We build a **single** Docker image containing all app code.
    * We deploy this same image to **10+ separate Cloud Run services**.
    * We control which app runs using an Environment Variable (`APP_NAME`).
* **Concurrency:** We tune the server to handle **80 concurrent students per instance** (vs default 1), drastically reducing the number of servers we pay for.

body:
## Overview

This PR introduces a complete decentralized auction system for real estate transactions on the Stacks blockchain. The implementation provides transparent property listing management and fair bidding mechanisms.

## Smart Contracts Added

### auction-listing.clar (254 lines)

Property registration and auction lifecycle management contract featuring:

- **Property Registration**: Register properties with complete metadata including title, description, location, and pricing parameters
- **Auction Status Management**: Track properties through pending, active, completed, and cancelled states
- **Time-based Controls**: Block-height-based auction start and end times
- **Seller Permissions**: Owner-only functions for starting, completing, and cancelling auctions
- **Property Metadata**: Additional property details including type, size, bedrooms, bathrooms, year built, and images
- **Query Functions**: Read-only access to property data, auction status, and time remaining

Key functions:
- `register-property`: Create new property listings with starting and reserve prices
- `set-property-metadata`: Add detailed property information
- `start-auction`: Activate auction with specified duration
- `complete-auction`: Finalize auction after end time
- `cancel-auction`: Cancel pending or active auctions
- `is-auction-active`: Check if auction is currently accepting bids
- `get-auction-time-remaining`: Calculate blocks until auction ends

### bid-engine.clar (266 lines)

Bidding logic and winner determination contract featuring:

- **Bid Placement**: Submit bids with automatic validation against minimum increments (5% increase)
- **Bid Tracking**: Complete history of all bids per property and per bidder
- **Highest Bid Management**: Real-time tracking of winning bid for each property
- **Bid Withdrawal**: Allow non-winning bidders to withdraw their bids
- **Winner Finalization**: Determine and record auction winners
- **Refund Calculation**: Calculate refund amounts for non-winning bidders

Key functions:
- `place-bid`: Submit a bid with automatic increment validation
- `withdraw-bid`: Withdraw non-winning bids
- `finalize-auction`: Record the final winner and winning amount
- `get-highest-bid`: Query current highest bid for a property
- `calculate-min-bid`: Compute minimum acceptable bid based on current highest
- `is-winning-bidder`: Check if a principal is the current highest bidder
- `get-bidder-refund-amount`: Calculate total refund amount for bidder

## Technical Details

- **No Cross-Contract Calls**: Both contracts operate independently for simplicity and security
- **Block-Height Timing**: Uses `stacks-block-height` for all time-based operations
- **Data Structure**: Efficient map-based storage for properties, bids, and relationships
- **Error Handling**: Comprehensive error constants for all failure scenarios
- **Read-Only Functions**: Gas-efficient query functions for UI integration

## Security Features

- Seller authorization checks on all property management functions
- Bid amount validation with minimum increment enforcement
- Prevention of withdrawal for current winning bids
- Status-based auction lifecycle enforcement
- Principal-based ownership verification

## Testing

Both contracts pass `clarinet check` validation with zero errors. The implementation includes TypeScript test scaffolding ready for comprehensive test coverage.

## Architecture

The system uses a two-contract architecture:
1. **auction-listing**: Manages the property inventory and auction configuration
2. **bid-engine**: Handles all bidding activity and winner determination

This separation ensures clean responsibilities and allows independent upgrades to either auction mechanics or bidding logic.

This pull request introduces significant improvements to both backend and frontend code related to expiration alerts and date scanning. The backend now provides expiration alerts for products that are either already expired or will expire within a configurable period, and the frontend refactors the date scanning workflow for better accuracy and user experience. Additionally, the frontend centralizes expiry-related logic for consistency in alert presentation.

### Backend: Expiry Alert Logic Improvements

* The method `get_alertas_caducidad_for_user` in `stock_repository.py` now includes both expired products and those expiring within the specified `days` period, instead of only future expirations. The query and documentation have been updated for clarity and correctness. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-6b4de84c1691ffe8ba9644eae353e1b4e1213a56f5a94ee87e55e5ca38c31dbfR39-R42) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-6b4de84c1691ffe8ba9644eae353e1b4e1213a56f5a94ee87e55e5ca38c31dbfL50-R56)
* The API endpoint in `alerts.py` now returns alerts for products expiring in the next 10 days or already expired, instead of the previous 7-day window.

### Frontend: Expiry Alert UI Consistency

* The alert dashboard in `main.dart` now uses centralized utility methods from `expiry_utils.dart` for determining expiry status, color, label, and message, ensuring consistent visual and textual feedback. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-199211b149f20d522739b584896968163ca3c6a4a98e9d285868546c11ce298bR14) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-199211b149f20d522739b584896968163ca3c6a4a98e9d285868546c11ce298bL98-R104) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-199211b149f20d522739b584896968163ca3c6a4a98e9d285868546c11ce298bL127-R125) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-199211b149f20d522739b584896968163ca3c6a4a98e9d285868546c11ce298bR147-R154) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-199211b149f20d522739b584896968163ca3c6a4a98e9d285868546c11ce298bL157-R173)

* The date scanner screen (`date_scanner_screen.dart`) has been refactored to use manual capture (single frame analysis) with maximum camera resolution for improved OCR accuracy, replacing the previous continuous stream approach. ## Description

- Modify error handling of the tilt sensor get_angle() funciton.
  - Try to reconnect to the tilt sensor if an error occurs in the get_angle().
- Change the logger level from `info` to `debug` in the `acq()` function to avoid a large amount of messages in loki outputs in grafana.

## Motivation and Context
<!--- Why is this change required? What problem does it solve? -->
<!--- If it fixes an open issue, please link to the issue here. -->
Sometimes, the connection to the tilt sensor was broken. To handle this automatically, I improved a reconnection process in the wiregrid tilt sensor agent.

To do this, I modified the error handling in the tilt sensor driver.
Previously, the agent attempted to reconnect only when get_angle() returned -999.
However, I found that get_angle() does not return -999 when the connection fails. Instead, it raises an error while reading data from the tilt sensor, and therefore, it does not return any value at all.

To trigger the reconnection when such an error occurs, I updated both `agents.py` and `drivers/dwl.py`.

author: claude[bot]
body:
## Summary
- Inspected `Cursor.java` and related pagination code
- Identified and eliminated redundant result limiting in cursor pagination
- All tests pass, behavior unchanged

## Area Inspected
Started with `src/main/java/spring/memewikibe/support/response/Cursor.java` and explored related files:
- `PageResponse.java`
- `MemeLookUpServiceImpl.java`
- `CursorTest.java`
- `PageResponseTest.java`

## Issues Found

### Code Duplication in Result Limiting
The `createPageResponseBy` method in `MemeLookUpServiceImpl` was limiting results **twice**:

1. **In the stream** (line 104):
   ```java
   List<MemeDetailResponse> response = memes.stream()
       .map(MemeDetailResponse::from)
       .limit(limit)  // First limiting
       .toList();
   ```

2. **In PageResponse.cursor()** (PageResponse.java line 15):
   ```java
   return new PageResponse<>(paging, results.subList(0, Math.min(results.size(), paging.getPageSize())));
   ```

This violated the design principle where `PageResponse.cursor()` is responsible for trimming results to match the cursor's `pageSize`.

## Changes Made

**File**: `src/main/java/spring/memewikibe/application/MemeLookUpServiceImpl.java`

Removed the redundant `.limit(limit)` from the stream:

```java
// Before
List<MemeDetailResponse> response = memes.stream()
    .map(MemeDetailResponse::from)
    .limit(limit)  // ← Removed this
    .toList();

// After
List<MemeDetailResponse> response = memes.stream()
    .map(MemeDetailResponse::from)
    .toList();
```

## Why This Improves the Code

1. **Eliminates Code Duplication**: Limiting logic now exists in only one place
2. **Centralizes Responsibility**: `PageResponse.cursor()` is clearly responsible for result trimming
3. **Better Separation of Concerns**: Service layer focuses on fetching and mapping; response layer handles pagination mechanics
4. **Maintains Correctness**: All existing tests pass, behavior is identical
5. **Cleaner Design**: Aligns with the existing test expectations in `PageResponseTest`

## Test Results

✅ All tests pass:
- `CursorTest`: Cursor metadata calculation
- `PageResponseTest`: Result trimming behavior
- `MemeLookUpServiceImpl` related tests: Pagination functionality

The test in `PageResponseTest.java` line 22-38 specifically validates this design:
- Input: 3 entities with limit 2, and 3 results
- Expected: `PageResponse.cursor()` trims to 2 results
- This confirms that result trimming is `PageResponse`'s responsibility

author: aurifi
body:
Previously if the dependency-track baseURL was under a subpath, client-go would ignore that subpath and therefore perform requests to nonexisting urls.

The reason for the defect is the behavior of URL.Parse, which uses URL.ResolveReference. From the [docs](https://pkg.go.dev/net/url#URL.ResolveReference):
> If ref is an absolute URL, then ResolveReference ignores base and returns a copy of ref.

Therefore if the leading slash is omitted both instances on the root of a domain aswell as Dependency Track deployed on a subpath will be supported.

author: mxschll
body:
**Note:** This PR supersedes [PR#3943](https://github.com/cloudscape-design/components/pull/3943) and includes an additional fix. The original implementation used `globalIndex` for the position offset calculation, which caused whitespace issues when scrolling through large lists:

```ts
// ./src/select/utils/render-options.tsx
const adjustedVirtualPosition = virtualItem ? virtualItem.start - globalIndex : undefined;
```

### Description

With virtual scrolling enabled, selectable items would "jump" on hover/selection due to border width changes (AWSUI-61303). Virtual scrolling positions items absolutely, so when border width changes from 1px to 2px on hover, the browser recalculates layout dimensions causing visible position shifts.

Additionally, option groups were missing the separating top border.

|  Before | After | 
|---|---|
| ![6ab8eb377aa9c0](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/387065be-5b38-4de9-8749-cf7cfcc8c2ce) | ![65b1c41442f210](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5c3fb82c-ed1a-4801-9c49-1e49012facb5) | 

The solution replaces borders and outlines with box-shadows to simulate borders while maintaining thin actual borders.

In summary: 

- Eliminates jumping behavior with virtual scrolling enabled
- Maintains visual consistency with non-virtual scrolling
- Adds top separator to option groups

### How has this been tested?

Changes ran through screenshot test and have been verified locally.

## Fix APEX System - Complete with Realistic Paper Trading, Champion Tracking & Frontend Integration

### ALL Changes Completed:
- [x] Remove synthetic/random data - use real HTX API
- [x] Add realistic paper trading (SL/TP, leverage, slippage, fees)
- [x] Add champion detail API endpoint for real-time tracking
- [x] Change branding from "Moon Dev" to "APEX" terminology
- [x] Query deduplication for strategy discovery
- [x] Frontend integration guide with working examples
- [x] **Moon-Dev code generation pattern integration**
- [x] **Fix duplicate logging issue**
- [x] **Instant-fix auto-debug for common errors**

### Realistic Paper Trading

**Before - Simple Simulation:**
```python
profit = risk_amount * np.random.uniform(1.5, 3.0)
```

**After - Realistic with Full Details:**
```python
# 3x leverage
position_size_usd = (risk_amount / stop_loss_pct) * 3.0
# Stop loss & take profit (2:1 RR)
stop_loss_price = entry_price * (1 - 0.02)
take_profit_price = entry_price * (1 + 0.04)
# Slippage (0.05%)
actual_entry = entry_price * (1 + 0.0005)
# HTX fees (0.2% taker)
entry_fee = position_size_usd * 0.002
exit_fee = position_size_usd * 0.002
# Final P&L
profit = pnl_before_fees - entry_fee - exit_fee - slippage_cost
```

**Trade Records Now Include:**
- Entry price, actual entry (with slippage), exit price
- Stop loss, take profit levels
- Position size (USD and units)
- Leverage used (3x), margin required
- Slippage cost, trading fees
- P&L before and after fees
- Confidence level

### Champion Detail API

**New Endpoint:** `GET /api/champion/{champion_id}`

Returns comprehensive champion data:
- **Bankroll**: current, initial, profit %, P&L, max/min P&L
- **Statistics**: total trades, win rate, trades today, daily win rate, avg profit, biggest win/loss
- **Recent Trades**: Last 50 trades with full details (entry, exit, SL, TP, fees, slippage, leverage)
- **Daily Performance**: Last 30 days with trades, wins, P&L per day
- **Eligibility**: Real trading status

### APEX Branding

Changed all "Moon Dev" references to "APEX":
- ✅ "APEX's Research AI 🚀"
- ✅ "APEX's Backtest AI 🚀"
- ✅ "APEX's Debug AI 🚀"
- ✅ "APEX's Optimization AI 🚀"
- ✅ "APEX themed debug prints"

### Frontend Integration Guide

**New File:** `FRONTEND_GUIDE.md`

Complete documentation for building the frontend dashboard:
- **API Documentation**: All endpoints with request/response examples
- **Quick Start Examples**: Vanilla JS, React, and Vue.js components ready to use
- **Champion Detail Page**: Full implementation with real-time trade tracking
- **Real-Time Updates**: Polling strategies (30s for lists, 10s for details)
- **Responsive Design**: Mobile-friendly CSS and layouts
- **Error Handling**: Production-ready patterns

**Key Features:**
- Copy-paste ready code examples in 3 frameworks
- Complete champion tracking UI with trade history
- Daily performance charts
- Real-time P&L updates
- Status badges (CHAMPION/ELITE/QUALIFIED)
- Profit/loss color coding

### Moon-Dev Code Generation Pattern

**System now follows Moon-Dev's proven backtest code structure:**

```python
def next(self):
    if entry_condition and not self.position:
        price = self.data.Close[-1]
        pos_size = 0.01  # 1% equity
        sl_price = price * (1 - self.stop_loss/100)
        tp_price = price * (1 + self.take_profit/100)

        self.buy(size=pos_size, sl=sl_price, tp=tp_price)  # Actual trade execution
```

**Key improvements:**

body:
This pull request introduces several improvements and refactors across authentication, error handling, and localization in both the app and web packages. The main focus is on streamlining authentication flows, improving error tracking, and enhancing internationalization support. It also removes redundant tests and updates dependencies for better stability and compatibility.

**Authentication and User Flow Improvements:**

* Refactored authentication logic to use new `signInEmail` and `signUpEmail` helper functions from `@repo/auth`, simplifying sign-in and sign-up actions and improving error handling. (`[[1]](diffhunk://#diff-d51ab3c5c33f10b1d607fceedb582629f5d10ac32f214a2d31224e2aa058408aL3-R24)`, `[[2]](diffhunk://#diff-a80940988535077899095f7386cf1a18b08a8700a91530f1676b8d09884a7faeL3-R5)`, `[[3]](diffhunk://#diff-12cd911ab603baacf21a00cd233d5c897a3a9205355a817ff97fe1247916a18cR20-R57)`)
* Added a new `requireUnauthenticatedUser` function to handle redirects for already authenticated users, and integrated it into unauthenticated layouts for better access control. (`[[1]](diffhunk://#diff-3c5df0fba0c0883ff173eb0887b90c46fe201b02016d409c74857a0fa2e9cce4L1-R14)`, `[[2]](diffhunk://#diff-aefd03c7338db57931083d1df080b6037d08cd8f6f66fd784ef60108b4a22074L3-R13)`, `[[3]](diffhunk://#diff-12cd911ab603baacf21a00cd233d5c897a3a9205355a817ff97fe1247916a18cR75-R84)`)
* Removed analytics identification from the authenticated layout and moved user identification to sign-in and sign-up actions for better separation of concerns. (`[[1]](diffhunk://#diff-f4b0235b524edeb57a72b9f73a82eefdf012a053116b39e3161079c22712df32L1)`, `[[2]](diffhunk://#diff-f4b0235b524edeb57a72b9f73a82eefdf012a053116b39e3161079c22712df32L12-L25)`, `[[3]](diffhunk://#diff-d51ab3c5c33f10b1d607fceedb582629f5d10ac32f214a2d31224e2aa058408aL3-R24)`, `[[4]](diffhunk://#diff-a80940988535077899095f7386cf1a18b08a8700a91530f1676b8d09884a7faeL13-L26)`)

**Error Tracking Enhancements:**

* Updated error tracking to use the unified `product.captureException` method instead of the older `analytics.captureException`, ensuring consistent error reporting in both app and web global error boundaries. (`[[1]](diffhunk://#diff-21f091a907345b5ee3b126f3cf0a8b15260c4c33b9a71dc2b861c94c874ec172L3-R5)`, `[[2]](diffhunk://#diff-21f091a907345b5ee3b126f3cf0a8b15260c4c33b9a71dc2b861c94c874ec172L16-R16)`, `[apps/web/app/[locale]/global-error.tsxL3-R3](diffhunk://#diff-6292248ac518de0239f8b72514785aa70c43610092bc017ffbab9da67bc80e69L3-R3)`, `[apps/web/app/[locale]/global-error.tsxL16-R16](diffhunk://#diff-6292248ac518de0239f8b72514785aa70c43610092bc017ffbab9da67bc80e69L16-R16)`)

**Internationalization and Localization:**

* Added `generateStaticParams` to the web app's locale layout to enable proper static generation for all supported languages, and removed redundant static params logic from the home page. (`[apps/web/app/[locale]/layout.tsxL5-R5](diffhunk://#diff-2d536abbc9f5867d1823149cd15ff7ca2668b2cde7a07a77bc12a87b564b83d6L5-R5)`, `[apps/web/app/[locale]/layout.tsxR16-R20](diffhunk://#diff-2d536abbc9f5867d1823149cd15ff7ca2668b2cde7a07a77bc12a87b564b83d6R16-R20)`, `[apps/web/app/[locale]/(home)/page.tsxL27-L31](diffhunk://#diff-38c83354d6bca923be6b74384d943b294e7387ca52ebcc26379d3ad9f3078a78L27-L31)`)

**Testing and Dependency Updates:**

* Removed outdated sign-in and sign-up page tests to clean up the test suite. (`[[1]](diffhunk://#diff-d0c958c17f883bbbdf1994e6962b7ac116c106d85e684a56c4ed293ba7351666L1-L8)`, `[[2]](diffhunk://#diff-87b0660598bfb32494a59ae63d88f5df4f98bc822673c0c070159c5cde98b9e5L1-L8)`)
* Updated various dependencies across packages for improved compatibility and security, including `vitest`, `fumadocs-core`, `chromatic`, and `@biomejs/biome`. (`[[1]](diffhunk://#diff-15a93da17a40a2a46b85fb22b881b4f9cf1e3df61f06826a7da6e7daa3ba0c66L43-R43)`, `[[2]](diffhunk://#diff-d03d2ce97fad5059ad6248fca5f5919994b09bca360f883318c03f1f817ae677L13-R15)`, `[[3]](diffhunk://#diff-d03d2ce97fad5059ad6248fca5f5919994b09bca360f883318c03f1f817ae677L31-R31)`, `[[4]](diffhunk://#diff-b6c0dcaee715dbce8821255c58de066b960ad35ecd820d5bd09f912543b4ee4cL37-R37)`, `[[5]](diffhunk://#diff-14b60f636e1a2b0061da57aaf231cb1ed15a5dc0c592425ed82e58fec95d42d8L19-R22)`, `[[6]](diffhunk://#diff-7ae45ad102eab3b6d7e7896acd08c427a9b25b346470d7bc6507b6481575d519L30-R43)`, `[[7]](diffhunk://#diff-1349f3412ff2498089104c031bcd07666359b8766bb1c4aef16f5ad1b49a2a4bL9-R9)`)

Critical fix implementing 3-mode system for BugReportModal:

**1. BugReportModal - 3 modos implementados:**
   - 'create': Crear nuevo bug (formulario vacío)
   - 'readonly': Ver bug existente (solo lectura, botón "View Full Details")
   - 'edit': Actualizar bug existente (formulario pre-llenado editable)

**2. TestRunnerModal (ejecución activa):**
   - Si NO hay bug: mode='create'
   - Si YA hay bug: mode='edit' ← FIX CRÍTICO

   - Toast: "actualizado" vs "reportado" según acción

**3. ExecutionDetailsModal (historial):**
   - Si NO hay bug: mode='create'
   - Si YA hay bug: mode='readonly' ← Correcto, sin cambios
   - Botón "View Full Details" navega a página de detalle

**4. BugReportModal changes:**
   - Prop mode: 'create' | 'readonly' | 'edit'
   - shouldLoadExistingBug: carga bug en readonly O edit mode
   - handleSubmit: POST (create) o PUT (edit) según modo
   - Título: "Report Bug" / "Update Bug" / "Bug Details"
   - Botón: "Create Bug Report" / "Update Bug Report" / "View Full Details"

**5. ScenarioCard:**
   - Ya actualizado: "View Bug (X)" cuando bugCount > 0
   - Tooltip: "Click para ver detalles"

All changes tested, build passes (0 TypeScript errors).

author: footballhead
body:
build.gradle uses copyTask to assemble assets inside build_android to pack into the APK. However, the CMake ppx_assets target is still being run which unnecessarily copies all assets into each CMake build dir in .cxx. Since there is one build dir for each (project, architecture) pair, there were many copies of unused data. This was wasting around 9GB of space (10 projects, 2 architectures, 450MB of assets).

A new CMake option controls whether ppx_assets is a dependency of the sample CMake targets. This is ON by default but set to OFF for the Gradle build.

Fixes: #582

author: corinedb
body:
In Laravel 11, the middleware() method was removed from the base Controller class. Middleware should be applied in routes or using Gate::authorize() in controller methods.

Changes:
- Removed $this->middleware() calls from constructor (causing the error)
- Added Gate::authorize() calls to all controller methods:
  - index(): voir_les_programmations
  - store(): creer_programmation
  - show(): voir_programmation
  - update(): modifier_programmation
  - destroy(): supprimer_programmation
- Added Illuminate\Support\Facades\Gate import

Routes already have auth:api middleware applied at the group level.

Fixes: "Call to undefined method ProgrammationController::middleware()"

author: philjb
body:
This brings several prs from enterprise into core. Most of volume is for improved error handling, but there are features:

* proper gzip multipayload support
* don't panic if there's an issue with the plugin dir
* improved resource not found messaging
* truncating user provided information in logging and errors
* cluster uuid header in all api responses

Ports most of or parts of
* https://github.com/influxdata/influxdb_pro/pull/1754 - `feat(http errors): improve error messages for not found`
* https://github.com/influxdata/influxdb_pro/pull/1684 - `refactor(http): centralize error handling through RoutingError enum`
* https://github.com/influxdata/influxdb_pro/pull/1683 - `feat(http): include cluster-uuid in response header for all requests`
* https://github.com/influxdata/influxdb_pro/pull/1670 - `chore(errors): refine errors and logging`
* https://github.com/influxdata/influxdb_pro/pull/1625 - `chore: improve error reporting for processing engine`
* https://github.com/influxdata/influxdb_pro/pull/1595 - `eat(server,http): accept multi-member gzip payloads`
* https://github.com/influxdata/influxdb_pro/pull/1371 - `feat: populate lvc dvc on creation`
* https://github.com/influxdata/influxdb_pro/pull/1100 - `fix: Error if plugin_dir is set with no pip/uv`

author: jaxofdiamonds
body:
# Summary

Adds *payee*, *amount*, and *transfer* arguments to the get_transactions function, allowing users to filter transactions.

## Motivation

This enables more targeted queries when working with transactions. This is a non-breaking approach.

## Changes

1. Updated get_transactions function with parameters (default values maintain backward compatibility) and conditional logic:
  - payee
  - amount
  - transfer

2. Test cases to cover various scenarios for the new paramaters.

| Package | Update | Change |

| [ghcr.io/home-operations/charts-mirror/openebs](https://www.openebs.io/) ([source](https://redirect.github.com/openebs/openebs)) | minor | `4.3.3` -> `4.4.0` |

---

### Release Notes

<details>
<summary>openebs/openebs (ghcr.io/home-operations/charts-mirror/openebs)</summary>

### [`v4.4.0`](https://redirect.github.com/openebs/openebs/releases/tag/v4.4.0)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/openebs/openebs/compare/v4.3.3...v4.4.0)

### OpenEBS 4.4.0 Release Notes

### Release Summary

OpenEBS version 4.4 introduces several functional fixes and new features focused on improving Data Security, User Experience, High availability (HA), replica rebuilds, and overall stability. The key highlights are LocalPV LVM snapshot restores . In addition, the release includes various usability and functional fixes for mayastor,  ZFS, LocalPV LVM and LocalPV Hostpath provisioners, along with documentation enhancements to help users and new contributors get started quickly.

### Replicated Storage (Mayastor)

#### New Features and Enhancements

- DiskPool Expansion
  It's now possible to expand a DiskPool's capacity by expanding the underlying storage device.

> ***NOTE***: As a precondition you must create the DiskPool with sufficient metadata to accommodate/support future growth, please read more about this [here](https://openebs.io/docs/main/user-guides/replicated-storage-user-guide/replicated-pv-mayastor/advanced-operations/diskpool-expansion).

- Configurable ClusterSize
  You can now configure the cluster size when creating a pool - larger cluster sizes may be beneficial when using very large storage devices.

> ***NOTE***: As an initial limitation volumes may not be placed across pools with different cluster sizes

- Pool Cordon
  Extend cordoning functionality to pools. This can be used to prevent new replicas from being created on a pool, and also as a way of migrating a volume replica out of it via scale-up/scale-down operations.
- Orphaned Retain Snapshot Delete
  Similar to volumes, when with snapshots retain move are deleted, the underlying storage is kept by the provisioner and must be deleted with provisioner specific commands.
  We've added a plugin sub-command to delete these orphaned snapshots safely.
- Node Spread
  Node spread topology may now be used
- Affinity Group ScaleDown
  Affinity group volumes may now be scaled down to 1 replica, provided the anti-affinity across nodes is not violated.

#### Bug Fixes and Improvements

- Update replica health as an atomic etcd transaction
- Exit io-engine with error if the gRPC port is busy
- Set PR\_SET\_IO\_FLUSHER for io-engine to resolve potential deadlock
- Don't let 1 bad nexus lockup the entire nexus subsystem
- Clean up uuid from DISKS output uri
- Honor stsAffinity on backup restores via external tools
- Validate K8s secret in diskpool operator ahead of pool creation request
- Allow pool creation with zfs volume paths
- Added support for kubeconfig context switching (kubectl-mayastor plugin)
- Fixed creating pools on very-slow/very-large storage devices
- Use udev kernel monitor
- Fixed race condition where udev events were lost leading to connecting nvme devices
- Fixed HA enablement on the latest rhel and derivatives
- Fixed open permissions on call-home encryption dir
- Configurable ports of services with hostNetwork
- Add support for 1GiB hugepages
- etcd dependency updated to `12.0.14`
- Use normalized etcdUrl in default etcd-probe init containers
- Use correct grpc port in metrics exporter
- Fix volume mkfs stuck on very large pools/volumes
- Fix agent-core panic when scheduling replicas
- Add default priority class to the daemon sets

#### Release Notes

- Refer to the [Mayastor v2.10.0 release](https://redirect.github.com/openebs/mayastor/releases/tag/v2.10.0) for detailed changes.

#### Limitations

- The Mayastor IO engine fully utilizes allocated CPU cores regardless of I/O load, running a poller at full speed.
- A Mayastor DiskPool is limited to a single block device and cannot span multiple block devices.
- The new at-rest encryption feature does not support rotating Data Encryption Keys(DEK).
- Volume rebuilds are only performed on published volumes.

#### Known Issues

- **IO-Engine Pod Restarts**
  - Under heavy I/O and during constant scaling up/down of volume replicas, the io-engine pod may restart occasionally.
- **fsfreeze Operation Failure**
  - If a pod-based workload is scheduled on a node that reboots and the pod lacks a controller (such as a Deployment or StatefulSet),  the volume unpublish operation might not be triggered.
  - This leads the control plane to assume the volume is still published, causing the fsfreeze operation to fail during snapshot creation.
    - **Workaround** Recreate or reinstate the pod to ensure proper volume mounting.
- **Diskpool's backing device failure**
  - If the backend device that hosts a diskpool runs into a fault, or gets removed e.g cloud disk removal, the status of diskpool and hosted replicas isn't clearly updated to reflect the problem.
  - As a result the resultant failures aren't gracefully handled and volume might remain Degraded for an extended period of time.
- **Extremely large pool undergoing dirty shutdown**
  - In case of a dirty shutdown of io-engine node hosting an extremely large pool e.g 10TiB or 20TiB.
  - The recovery of pool takes a while after the node comes online.

### LocalPV ZFS

#### New Features and Enhancements

- Update Go runtime to 1.24.
  Bumps up go runtime and all dependents to their latest available releases
- Allow users to configure CPU and memory requests/limits for all zfs-node and zfs-controller containers via values.yaml, improving resource management and deployment flexibility

#### Bug Fixes and Improvements

- Removes encryption parameter handling from `buildCloneCreateArgs()` since clones automatically inherit encryption from the parent snapshot and the property cannot be set (it's read-only)

#### Continuous Integration and Maintenance

- Staging CI
  Introduction of the staging CI, which enables creating a staging build for e2e testing before releasing, the artifacts are then copied over to production build hosts.

#### Release Notes

- Refer to the [ZFS v2.9.0 release](https://redirect.github.com/openebs/zfs-localpv/releases/tag/v2.9.0) for detailed changes.

### LocalPV LVM

#### New Features and Enhancements

- Snapshot restore
  LocalPV-LVM snapshot had limited capabilities. Now we support restoring a snapshot to volume
- ThinPool space reclamation
  LocalPV-LVM will cleanup the thinpool LV after deleting the last thin volume of the thinpool
- Scheduler fixes and enhancements
  Record thinpool statistics in lvmnode CR. Fail fast CreateVolume request if thick PVC size cannot be accommodated by any VG.
  Considers thinpool free space while scheduling thin pvc in SpaceWeighted algorithm
- Runtime improvements

author: jakechirsch
body:
- Closes #62840 

This PR adds a new `threshold` argument to `to_datetime` that allows users to specify the minimum fraction of valid datetime components required for parsing to succeed. For this feature, "successful" parsing means that the function returns either a valid `Timestamp` or `NaT` (i.e., it does not raise an exception). The threshold determines whether partially-invalid values produce `NaT` or raise an error. This enables more flexible and robust parsing behavior for partially-invalid dates while preserving strict behavior by default (`threshold=1.0`).

### Summary of changes
- Added `threshold` argument to `to_datetime`.
- Implemented validation logic and clamping of threshold values to `[0.0, 1.0]`.
- Updated parsing internals to compute the fraction of valid components.
- Added tests for valid, invalid, and boundary threshold behavior.
- Added documentation: explanation, parameter description, and example.
- Added type annotations across all new argument signatures.
- Ensured all code checks and pre-commit hooks pass.

author: xuechendi
body:
SW-241080

**Current status:**
   UA + spec_decode NGRAM => Done => accuracy verified
   UA + spec_decode eagle3 => Done => accuracy verified

**design doc:**
For non-UA, we will pad target_model input to fix token_ids shape to limit potential hpu graph possibility
For UA, we can use actual draft token to avoid redundant padding => follow very similar design as GPU does

Which is to say, For UA spec decode:
1. we skip spec decode for target model if non_draft_tokens generated from last run
2. with draft token, do not pad input_token_ids, use target_token_indices and bonus_token_indices to indicate tokens for reject sampler to judge
3. However, for inupt to draft model, we will reuse attn_metadata from target model(as initial impl) => update meta to remove rejected token will be next step.

```
# Example:
      # scheduled_spec_decode_tokens={'0': [-1], '1': [-1], '2': [17689], '3': [-1]} => only 3rd request has draft token
      # token_ids = [[tok_0], [tok_1], [tok_2, draft_tok], [tok_4]]
      # draft_token_indices = [0, 0, 3, 0] => pos of token_ids for compare to target model output
      # target_token_indices = [-1, -1, 2, -1] => -1 is place holder, only verify pos==2 of target model output
      # bonus_token_indices = [0, 1, 3, 4] => new generated token from target model

      # current design for draft model fwd
      # say if target token gets verified by target model
      # => last token indices to select draft token from draft model is [0, 1, 3, 4]
      # say if target token gets rejected
      # => last token indices select draft token from from draft model is [0, 1, 2, 4]     
```

**workflow:**
== start step ==
input(contains prompt, no draft) => target_model => regular sampling => update states => draft model => update draft token for next step

== next step ==
input(contains draft tokens) => target_model (use sharable attn with multiple tokens in one req - token + draft tokens) => rejection sampler (verify draft tokens to get final validated sampled tokens) => update states => draft model (to get new draft tokens, we need to skip any tokens rejected by target model) => update draft token for next step
Example:
input is 
input with draft is                            [[in your]      [is]   [nice tool] [name]] 
=> output from target model is     [[your mind] [an] [way used] [name]] 
=> after rejection sampler              [[your mind] [an] [way]         [name]]   // only accept bonus token when draft accepeted
=> input to draft model                  [[mind]         [an] [way]         [name]]  // notice, we need to create new attn_meta or reuse existing but calfully select output indices. 


**Changes introduced in this PR**
1. add new arg for spec decode to `create_unified_batch`
2. update `unified_execute_model` UPDATE REQUEST STATE part, so draft token can be picked by scheduler
4. shift parameters `propose_draft_token_ids` so we can make several arguments with default values
5. implement new `_prepare_spec_decode_inputs_for_ua` for Unified Attention preparation
6. Add new propose_eagle_unified with new proposal file


**Validation:**
```
VLLM_UNIFIED_ATTN=True VLLM_SKIP_WARMUP=True PT_HPU_LAZY_MODE=1 python "${VLLM_GAUDI_PREFIX}/tests/full_tests/spec_decode.py" --task ngram --assert_acc_rate 0.25 --osl 512
and
```

```javascript
  payer_phone: telefono    // ← Maps to payer.phone.number
```

author: ehpor
body: Fixes #293. Adds the ability to use custom colormaps for complex fields. The default hsv colormap is retained. Test script: ```python import hcipy import numpy as np import matplotlib.pyplot as plt import cmocean grid = hcipy.make_pupil_grid(1024, 5) a = np.sinc(grid.as_('polar').r) * np.exp(10j * grid.x) a.grid = grid plt.figure(figsize=(6, 6)) plt.subplot(2, 2, 1) plt.title('hsv + dark') hcipy.imshow_field(a, cmap='hsv', theme='dark') plt.subplot(2, 2, 2) plt.title('hsv + light') hcipy.imshow_field(a, cmap='hsv', theme='light') plt.subplot(2, 2, 3) plt.title('cmocean:phase + dark') hcipy.imshow_field(a, cmap=cmocean.cm.phase, theme='dark') plt.subplot(2, 2, 4) plt.title('cmocean:phase + light') hcipy.imshow_field(a, cmap=cmocean.cm.phase, theme='light') plt.show() ```
